passages.text: How beautiful are your sandaled feet, O daughter of the prince! The curves of your thighs are like jewels, the handiwork of a master.
passages.sermon:
The speaker addresses a woman called the daughter of a prince.
The speaker admires her.
Your feet are beautiful in sandals.
The curves of your thighs are like jewels.
A skilled craftsman made them.
passages.original: מַה־ יָּפ֧וּ פְעָמַ֛יִךְ בַּנְּעָלִ֖ים בַּת־ נָדִ֑יב חַמּוּקֵ֣י יְרֵכַ֔יִךְ כְּמ֣וֹ חֲלָאִ֔ים מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יְדֵ֥י אָמָּֽן׃

passages.text: Your navel is a rounded goblet; it never lacks blended wine. Your waist is a mound of wheat encircled by the lilies.
passages.sermon:
The speaker addresses the Shulammite woman.
The speaker describes her body with admiration.
Your navel is like a rounded goblet.
This goblet always has mixed wine in it.
Your waist is like a mound of wheat.
Lilies surround this mound of wheat.
passages.original: שָׁרְרֵךְ֙ אַגַּ֣ן הַסַּ֔הַר אַל־ יֶחְסַ֖ר הַמָּ֑זֶג בִּטְנֵךְ֙ עֲרֵמַ֣ת חִטִּ֔ים סוּגָ֖ה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים׃

passages.text: Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.
passages.sermon:
The speaker addresses a woman.
The speaker describes her beauty.
Her breasts are soft and gentle.
They are like two young fawns.
The fawns are twins.
The fawns are from a gazelle.
passages.original: שְׁנֵ֥י שָׁדַ֛יִךְ כִּשְׁנֵ֥י עֳפָרִ֖ים תָּאֳמֵ֥י צְבִיָּֽה׃

passages.text: Your neck is like a tower made of ivory; your eyes are like the pools of Heshbon by the gate of Bath-rabbim; your nose is like the tower of Lebanon, facing toward Damascus.
passages.sermon:
The beloved woman is the subject.
Her neck is tall and beautiful.
Her neck is like a tower made of ivory.
Her eyes are clear and deep.
Her eyes are like the pools of Heshbon.
These pools are by the gate of Bath-rabbim.
Her nose is strong and noble.
Her nose is like the tower of Lebanon.
This tower faces toward Damascus.
passages.original: צַוָּארֵ֖ךְ כְּמִגְדַּ֣ל הַשֵּׁ֑ן עֵינַ֜יִךְ בְּרֵכ֣וֹת בְּחֶשְׁבּ֗וֹן עַל־ שַׁ֙עַר֙ בַּת־ רַבִּ֔ים אַפֵּךְ֙ כְּמִגְדַּ֣ל הַלְּבָנ֔וֹן צוֹפֶ֖ה פְּנֵ֥י דַמָּֽשֶׂק׃

passages.text: Your head crowns you like Mount Carmel, the hair of your head like purple threads; the king is captured in your tresses.
passages.sermon:
The woman is beautiful.
Her head sits above her like Mount Carmel.
Her hair is like threads of purple.
A king is caught in her hair.
passages.original: רֹאשֵׁ֤ךְ עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ כַּכַּרְמֶ֔ל וְדַלַּ֥ת רֹאשֵׁ֖ךְ כָּאַרְגָּמָ֑ן מֶ֖לֶךְ אָס֥וּר בָּרְהָטִֽים׃

passages.text: How fair and pleasant you are, O love, with your delights!
passages.sermon:
The speaker addresses his beloved woman.
He sees her beauty.
He says she is beautiful.
He says she is pleasant.
He calls her "love."
He says she brings delights.
passages.original: מַה־ יָּפִית֙ וּמַה־ נָּעַ֔מְתְּ אַהֲבָ֖ה בַּתַּֽעֲנוּגִֽים׃

passages.text: Your stature is like a palm tree; your breasts are clusters of fruit.
passages.sermon:
The woman stands tall and upright.
Her body is graceful and strong.
She is like a palm tree.
Her breasts are full and beautiful.
They are like clusters of fruit.
passages.original: זֹ֤את קֽוֹמָתֵךְ֙ דָּֽמְתָ֣ה לְתָמָ֔ר וְשָׁדַ֖יִךְ לְאַשְׁכֹּלֽוֹת׃

passages.text: I said, “I will climb the palm tree; I will take hold of its fruit.” May your breasts be like clusters of the vine, the fragrance of your breath like apples, and your mouth like the finest wine. May it flow smoothly to my beloved, gliding gently over lips and teeth.
passages.sermon:
A man speaks to the woman he loves.
He says, “I will climb the palm tree.
I will take hold of its fruit.”
He desires her beauty.
He says, “May your breasts be like clusters of the vine.
May the fragrance of your breath be like apples.
May your mouth be like the finest wine.
May this wine flow smoothly to my beloved.
May it glide gently over lips and teeth.”
passages.original: אָמַ֙רְתִּי֙ אֶעֱלֶ֣ה בְתָמָ֔ר אֹֽחֲזָ֖ה בְּסַנְסִנָּ֑יו וְיִֽהְיוּ־ נָ֤א שָׁדַ֙יִךְ֙ כְּאֶשְׁכְּל֣וֹת הַגֶּ֔פֶן וְרֵ֥יחַ אַפֵּ֖ךְ כַּתַּפּוּחִֽים׃ וְחִכֵּ֕ךְ כְּיֵ֥ין הַטּ֛וֹב הוֹלֵ֥ךְ לְדוֹדִ֖י לְמֵישָׁרִ֑ים דּוֹבֵ֖ב שִׂפְתֵ֥י יְשֵׁנִֽים׃

passages.text: I belong to my beloved, and his desire is for me.
passages.sermon: The woman speaks.\r\nShe says, “I belong to my beloved.”\r\nShe says, “My beloved desires me.”

passages.text: Come, my beloved, let us go to the countryside; let us spend the night among the wildflowers.
passages.sermon:
The woman speaks to her beloved.
She says, "Come, my beloved."
She invites him to go with her to the countryside.
She asks him to spend the night with her among the villages and wildflowers.
passages.original: לְכָ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ נֵצֵ֣א הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה נָלִ֖ינָה בַּכְּפָרִֽים׃

passages.text: Let us go early to the vineyards to see if the vine has budded, if the blossom has opened, if the pomegranates are in bloom— there I will give you my love.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a woman who loves her beloved deeply.
She invites her beloved to go with her.
She says, "Let us go early to the vineyards."
She wants to see if the vine has budded.
She wants to see if the blossom has opened.
She wants to see if the pomegranates are in bloom.
She promises her beloved, "There I will give you my love."
passages.original: נַשְׁכִּ֙ימָה֙ לַכְּרָמִ֔ים נִרְאֶ֞ה אִם פָּֽרְחָ֤ה הַגֶּ֙פֶן֙ פִּתַּ֣ח הַסְּמָדַ֔ר הֵנֵ֖צוּ הָרִמּוֹנִ֑ים שָׁ֛ם אֶתֵּ֥ן אֶת־ דֹּדַ֖י לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: The mandrakes send forth a fragrance, and at our door is every delicacy, new as well as old, that I have treasured up for you, my beloved.
passages.sermon:
The mandrakes give a sweet smell.
Every kind of delicacy lies at our door.
There are new delicacies.
There are also old delicacies.
I have saved these for you, my beloved.
passages.original: הַֽדּוּדָאִ֣ים נָֽתְנוּ־ רֵ֗יחַ וְעַל־ פְּתָחֵ֙ינוּ֙ כָּל־ מְגָדִ֔ים חֲדָשִׁ֖ים גַּם־ יְשָׁנִ֑ים דּוֹדִ֖י צָפַ֥נְתִּי לָֽךְ׃
